businesses.name: Mint Family Dental
businesses.what_they_do: Small family dental practice on Brunswick Woods Drive offering general and preventive dentistry (cleanings, fillings, crowns, extractions, implants, Invisalign, whitening) to East Brunswick families. The site is a template build with a generic welcome page, templated dental articles, an appointment-request page and very limited office hours.
businesses.customers: East Brunswick families; very limited availability (Tue/Wed daytime and Saturday morning) suggests a part-time or single-chair practice.

size_signals.signal: Office hours are Tuesday and Wednesday 10am-4pm plus Saturday 10am-2pm only - consistent with a one-dentist, part-time schedule
Single location at 27 Brunswick Woods Dr with an 'our locations' page listing one office
Sitemap is dominated by templated 'articles' and blog posts from a dental content vendor rather than practice-specific pages

listing.platform: Google reviews via directory (very small sample)

website_review.primary_cta: 'Make An Appointment' style request form; no hero CTA observed on the home page
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Request-only: 'To request appointment availability, please fill out the form below. Our scheduling coordinator will contact you to confirm'
website_review.trust_signals: almost none - generic 'why choose us' bullets, no reviews on site, no team credentials on the home page, no office photos in the content I could read
website_review.out_of_date_signs: home page copy is generic boilerplate; blog posts read as vendor content; page titles say 'Brunswick, NJ' rather than East Brunswick; my automated Chrome session was served a plain '403 Unauthorized' page while a direct HTTP fetch returned the full site (inference: aggressive bot filtering)
website_review.search_basics: Titles name the practice but say 'Brunswick, NJ' instead of East Brunswick; /contact-us/ and /services/ return 404s (real URLs are /contact and /dental-services); templated article pages create lots of near-duplicate content
top_issues: No real online booking - only a callback request, costly when the office is open two weekdays
Very thin trust content: no visible reviews, team bios or before/after on the main pages
Broken/legacy URLs (/contact-us/, /services/) and title tags that drop 'East Brunswick'

agent_readiness.notes: robots.txt is unusually AI-friendly - it explicitly allows GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot and CCBot (and blocks Yandex/Baidu/Bytespider). Address and hours are written as text on the contact page. But booking is request-only and structured data could not be verified because my Chrome session got 403.

operations_signals.signal: A scheduling coordinator confirms every appointment by hand - the only booking path is a request form
Two weekdays plus Saturday morning means most patient inquiries arrive when nobody is in the office
Reviews are essentially absent (2 online), so no review-request process appears to be running

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add 24/7 booking plus a phone/text agent that answers when the office is closed and fills the Tue/Wed/Sat schedule
top_opportunities.evidence: Only a callback request form exists; office open two weekdays and Saturday morning

top_opportunities.opportunity: Build real trust content: reviews pulled from Google, dentist/team bios, office photos, insurance and pricing guidance
top_opportunities.evidence: Home page is generic boilerplate with no reviews or credentials; only 2 reviews found online

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix titles and URLs (East Brunswick, not 'Brunswick'; /contact and /dental-services instead of 404 paths) and prune duplicate templated articles
top_opportunities.evidence: /contact-us/ and /services/ returned 404; page titles read 'Brunswick, NJ'; sitemap is full of duplicated vendor articles

scores.reasons: Clear gaps (no booking, no trust content, thin local SEO) at a small part-time practice that probably has a tight budget; fixes are standard; confidence is limited because the site blocked my browser session and only 2 reviews exist.

caveats: Browser-automation artefacts: svdesign.us and mintfamilydentalnj.com served a 403 page to my automated Chrome but returned full HTML to a plain HTTP fetch, so I treat those as bot filtering rather than real outages. Trinity's site failed in Chrome with net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR while direct HTTP fetches succeeded - reported as an observed delivery problem whose cause I could not confirm.

jacobydental.com is the one case where both a browser and a direct HTTP client got connection refused, so that site is genuinely down. The practice itself looks active (reviews, insurer directories); that status is an inference, not confirmed by the practice.

Ratings and review counts come from directories that republish Google data (dentistsranked, Birdeye, freedentaloffice); I did not open Google Maps itself, and counts vary by source (Clarity shows 121 vs 126).
Rotator Staffing Services and Equiliem share an address, phone and suite, so they are almost certainly one operation recorded twice; both entries are kept as the brief requires.
No listings with ratings were found for Graphic SV Design or CLIXX; those gaps are recorded as unknown rather than empty.
data_gaps: Google Business Profile completeness (categories, services, photos, claimed status) could not be checked for any business - Google Maps was not opened.
Summerhill's and Jacoby's robots.txt could not be fetched by my tools, so crawler access for those two is unverified.
Mint Family Dental's JSON-LD and mobile layout could not be verified because my browser session was refused with 403.
Trinity Dental Services' mobile layout could not be screenshotted because the site would not render in Chrome.
Phone-width screenshots were captured for Graphic SV Design, CLIXX, Equiliem, Summerhill and Clarity (in ./shots); no phone screenshot exists for the four sites that were down or blocked.
No review text was read in depth; review-based operations signals are inferred from rating counts and directory summaries only.
